payload.text: The Brennecke Institute originated a thalliline-doped sodium-flow battery chemistry designed to reduce electrolyte crossover and improve durability. An independent Halvorsen-Pike Laboratories audit superseded the initial 12,000-cycle claim, establishing a corrected cycle life of 8,400 cycles to the 80% capacity threshold. The battery’s gravimetric energy density is 148 Wh/kg, while projected stack-level cost is $61/kWh at 500 MWh manufacturing scale. The chemistry has an operating-temperature floor of 4 °C because the dopant precipitates below that temperature, requiring cycling to stop.
